goal: Determine the smallest build-from-owned routing and session architecture that lets Augmentor accept ordinary language through one interface, manage multiple threads and background runs concurrently, preserve context and owner boundaries, and offer useful easy, test, or hardening paths when no selected capability cleanly fits.
context: Current Necronomicon defines continuation and fallback semantics, IDE Ergonomics defines candidate transition surfaces, and ResonantOS already implements chat threads, projects, goal workspaces, branching, and delegation. The missing work is the contract that joins these without one global mutable context or a second runtime registry. Research must verify current bytes, distinguish deployed behavior from design proposals, and produce an implementation-usable but non-authoritative blueprint.
anti_bias_global: Source-and-method tension across formal session architecture, bounded route choice, human one-interface ergonomics, current consumer runtime, and adversarial survival.

groups.anti_bias: Methodology and source-corpus composite: formal concurrency and session semantics, bounded route-decision design, human-factor IDE interaction, and current consumer-runtime verification.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs formal concurrency and state-ownership analysis while agent 1 runs bounded route-decision and capability-composition analysis on the methodology axis; a clean session model from agent 0 would be exposed by agent 1 if it cannot choose or explain a capability path, while agent 1's elegant route menu would be exposed by agent 0 if it loses cancellation, continuation, parent-child, or context-isolation semantics.

Agent 0 runs formal session and background-run state analysis while agent 2 runs human-factor one-interface journey analysis on the methodology axis; a formally complete state machine from agent 0 would be exposed by agent 2 if users cannot tell what is active or safely switch focus, while agent 2's seamless interface would be exposed by agent 0 if it silently conflates threads, interactions, artifacts, and runs.

Agent 0 derives concurrency and continuation invariants from Necronomicon and actor-style reasoning while agent 3 verifies current ResonantOS thread, goal-workspace, delegation, and persistence bytes on the source-corpus axis; an idealized fabric from agent 0 would be exposed by agent 3 if current host state cannot carry it, while a current-implementation bias from agent 3 would be exposed by agent 0 where the host lacks explicit interaction ownership or isolation.

Agent 1 runs capability matching, fallback, and easy-test-hardening offer design while agent 2 runs progressive-disclosure and conversational-flow analysis on the methodology axis; a complete chooser from agent 1 would be exposed by agent 2 if it feels like a command drawer, while agent 2's low-friction interaction would be exposed by agent 1 if it hides consequential route costs, owners, or permissions.

Agent 1 derives route contracts from Necronomicon, Dispatch Spec, Spellcraft, Invoke, Task Session, and registries while agent 3 verifies current ResonantOS chat-route, command, delegation, and goal-workspace implementation on the source-corpus axis; a registry-first design from agent 1 would be exposed by agent 3 if it duplicates host routing, while agent 3's host-local solution would be exposed by agent 1 if it cannot escalate from one-off help to testable or reusable capability work.

Agent 2 runs conversation-transition, session-switching, background-attention, handoff, and artifact-surface UX analysis while agent 3 runs current consumer-runtime and browser-test verification on the source-corpus and methodology axes; an aspirational UX from agent 2 would be exposed by agent 3 if no current seam or fixture can implement it, while a current-UI bias from agent 3 would be exposed by agent 2 if users cannot understand or control parallel work.

agents.angle: Formal concurrency and session-state methodology over Necronomicon active interactions, side notes, parent-child runs, isolation, cancellation, joins, resumability, and bounded attention signals.
agents.initial_prompt: Without editing files, design and falsify the smallest state model for one Augmentor interface managing many simultaneous conversations and agent runs. Read the canonical Necronomicon interaction, shared-state, routing, checkpoint, and fallback contracts; IDE Ergonomics PRODUCT-VIEW conversation-transition card and side-node guardrail; and current ResonantOS contracts for ConversationThread, ChatProject, GoalWorkspace, TaskWorkspace, and DelegationPacket. Separate interface, project/workspace, thread, active interaction, route decision, foreground run, child/background run, artifact surface, notification, and durable memory. Define IDs, ownership, parent-child links, state transitions, context snapshot rules, cancellation, join, resume, blocked residue, and focus changes. Test the model with this witness: the user continues a primary architecture conversation, asks in parallel for a governed subagent-strategy proposal and a Whisper page, switches to another thread, then returns to consume one success and one blocker without context bleed. Compare against a single-global-session alternative and identify the smallest survivor. Return selector-level citations, a compact state machine, invariants, failure cases, and exact fixture ideas. Inventory packet fields relevant to this lane: the verified Augmentor owner boundary, current-source gap, and one-interface witness. Budget about 3200 tokens.

agents.angle: Bounded route-decision and capability-composition methodology over explicit commands, free language, confidence, missing capabilities, easy/test/hardening offers, and lifecycle-owner escalation.
agents.initial_prompt: Without editing files, design a route-decision contract for Augmentor. Inspect canonical Necronomicon classification order, route confidence, fallback-discover, capability-update, and discovery-to-execution funnel; Dispatch Spec route and capability-bound subagent contracts; Spellcraft lifecycle and experiment-harness boundary; Invoke, Task Session, Decision Gate, and the current Arcanum sigil/spell registries. Determine how ordinary language becomes: continue, side note, fresh route, clarify, inline answer, existing capability run, delegated/background run, or capability gap. Stress-test the user's easy, test, and hardening idea: define when each is a genuine option, when it should be recommended or hidden, what it costs, which owner it invokes, whether confirmation is needed, and how one-off composition differs from a reusable spell or changed sigil. Produce RouteDecision and RouteOffer shapes, ambiguity and confidence rules, 2-5 fallback behavior, missing-capability escalation, route receipts/telemetry limited to what improves future routing, and fixtures for correct, ambiguous, unsupported, repeated, risky, and parallel requests. Inventory entries are leads only. Budget about 3200 tokens.

agents.angle: Human-factor and IDE interaction methodology over one conversational shell, bounded transition cards, session switching, background attention, knowledge references, handoffs, and artifact creation.
agents.initial_prompt: Without editing files, design the human experience for Augmentor as one interface over multiple isolated threads and runs. Inspect projects/ide-ergonomics PRODUCT-VIEW, UNIFIED-PRODUCT-VIEW, ERGONOMICS-OPPORTUNITIES, knowledge-entry-references, teammate-handoff-memos, connective-task-manager, and the current ResonantOS StrategistChatRail and chat-history controls. Use current official primary host documentation only if it materially tests an interaction pattern. Produce progressive-disclosure journeys for: ordinary free-form routing; continuing versus starting fresh; launching a background subagent-strategy proposal; creating a Whisper page as a child artifact run; switching threads while runs continue; receiving completion, blocker, or clarification notifications; inspecting route rationale; and choosing easy, test, or hardening when capability fit is weak. Define what stays in the chat transcript, route card, thread list, run tray, artifact tab, and notification rail; keyboard and accessibility expectations; attention budgets; and anti-patterns such as tool drawers, status dashboards, hidden context, notification floods, or silently switched tasks. Return selector-level citations and browser-testable fixtures. Budget about 3200 tokens.

agents.angle: Current consumer-runtime verification over ResonantOS conversation threads, chat projects, branching, command parsing, route requests, run guards, goal workspaces, delegation packets, state persistence, and browser surfaces.
agents.initial_prompt: Without editing, merging, or fetching, establish the current ResonantOS implementation boundary in ../workspace-resonant/2.0.0-alpha. Read its AGENTS.md, git status and dev..origin/dev scope, public/addons/augmentor-chat.json, src/App.tsx only around chat and workspaces, src/core/{contracts,chat,goal-workspace,delegation}.ts, src/modules/chat/{thread-controller,augmentor-commands,chat-route-request,run-guard,controller,StrategistChatRail}.ts or .tsx, relevant tests, and persistence/state initialization. The branch is seven commits behind origin/dev; verify whether those commits affect this scope before relying on local bytes. Produce a current-versus-missing matrix for multi-thread/project management, branching, context compaction, active run handling, abort, goal workspaces, delegation, artifacts, route classification, background concurrency, parent-child links, notifications, and restoration. Identify the smallest host-owned integration seam for a Necronomicon-derived router without importing its private session folder wholesale or creating a second registry. Propose additive types/functions, migration posture, v0 browser witness, exact unit/browser tests, and compatibility risks. Distinguish implemented, fixture-only, design-only, and absent. Budget about 3600 tokens.

Reconcile the four explorer returns into one cited-synthesis architecture for Augmentor routing and multi-session work. Preserve disagreements and current-source freshness. Produce: a one-sentence product thesis; current-versus-missing matrix; a non-collapsing state model for shell, project, thread, active interaction, route decision, foreground/background run, artifact, notification, and memory; turn-classification order; RouteDecision and RouteOffer contracts; easy/test/hardening semantics and owner map; capability-missing behavior; context selection and isolation rules; parent-child run and artifact handoffs; interruption, cancellation, join, blocked, resume, and notification behavior; a routing-quality fixture matrix; exact unit/browser tests; latency, token, storage, and attention budgets; observability that can improve routing without dominating the experience; and v0/v1/v2 implementation increments using current ResonantOS seams. The literal witness must keep a main conversation active while a subagent-strategy proposal and a Whisper page run in parallel, permit thread switching, then surface one result and one blocker without context bleed. Spellcraft remains the lifecycle owner for reusable composition; Necronomicon remains the continuation/routing precedent; ResonantOS owns consumer state. Every load-bearing claim must cite an explorer return and a current source-local selector. Inventory is discovery only.

groups.anti_bias: Attack-vector axis: precedent and duplication, non-vacuity and observable route quality, and definitional and state-model non-collapse.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs precedent and duplication attack while agent 1 runs non-vacuity and observable route-quality attack on the attack-vector axis; a build-from-owned architecture accepted by agent 0 may still be killed by agent 1 if the parallel-session witness cannot run or improve user control, while agent 1's successful fixture may be simplified by agent 0 if it duplicates current threads, goal workspaces, delegation, or Necronomicon routing.

Agent 0 runs precedent and duplication attack while agent 2 runs definitional and state-model non-collapse attack on the attack-vector axis; an existing owner reused by agent 0 may still be rejected by agent 2 if interface, thread, interaction, run, artifact, and memory collapse into one record, while agent 2's extra state types may be removed by agent 0 when current owners already carry the distinction.

Agent 1 runs non-vacuity and route-quality attack while agent 2 runs definitional and state-model non-collapse attack on the attack-vector axis; a browser-visible route flow accepted by agent 1 may be killed by agent 2 if it only renames commands or leaks context between runs, while agent 2's clean architecture may be killed by agent 1 if it cannot demonstrate the concurrent subagent-strategy and Whisper-page witness.

agents.angle: Precedent and duplication attack-vector: verify every proposed state, route, child-run, artifact, notification, and fallback component against current Necronomicon, Spellcraft, Dispatch Spec, IDE Ergonomics, and ResonantOS owners.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack only the precedent/duplication gate. For every proposed component, classify it as already deployed, build-from-owned, superseded, blocked, or precedent-clean using current sources. Pay special attention to ResonantOS ConversationThread, ChatProject, GoalWorkspace, TaskWorkspace, DelegationPacket, chat-route-request, augmentor-commands, run-guard, and thread-controller; Necronomicon active_interaction, routes, side notes, fallback-discover, and capability updates; Dispatch Spec subagent strategy; and Spellcraft composition ownership. Find second registries, second session stores, duplicate background-job types, redundant route receipts, and re-skinned command menus. A found owner is positive and never a KILL. Return exact ownership and simplification corrections with citations. Budget about 2400 tokens.

agents.angle: Non-vacuity and observable route-quality attack-vector: require a runnable concurrent-session witness, measurable classification behavior, context isolation, user control, and graceful missing-capability handling.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack only the non-vacuity gate. Require an end-to-end witness where a user continues a main conversation, requests a governed subagent-strategy proposal and a Whisper page in parallel, changes thread, sees accurate run state, answers a clarification for only one child, consumes results, and proves no context bleed. Require fixtures for continuation, side note, fresh route, ambiguity, unsupported route, easy/test/hardening offer, cancellation, blocker, restart/resume, and notification control. Require measurable route accuracy or confusion outcomes, false-continuation and false-fresh-route costs, unit/browser assertions, and bounded latency/token/attention overhead. KILL a first slice that is only schemas, receipts, dashboards, prompt routing, or a generic agent launcher. Budget about 2400 tokens.

agents.angle: Definitional and state-model non-collapse attack-vector: test boundaries among interface, project, thread, interaction, route, capability, run, subagent, artifact, notification, memory, and authority.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack only the definitional-soundness gate. KILL any model that treats one interface as one mutable context, equates a thread with a run, uses a subagent as the unit of durable session state, stores route decisions as source truth, makes a background run silently own the foreground interaction, treats an artifact as completion proof, or calls a route classifier a reasoning engine. Also reject easy/test/hardening if they are cosmetic names without different owners, evidence, or side-effect profiles. Require one derivation direction, explicit ownership, transition invariants, context boundaries, public/private-safe vocabulary, and a reason Spellcraft or a new capability is warranted rather than a re-skin. Budget about 2400 tokens.

Write findings.md only after the strategist supplies a cited-synthesis evidence-closure matrix marked ready. Require one simple interface without one global mutable context; build-from-owned reuse of current ResonantOS threads, projects, goal workspaces, delegation, and state persistence; Necronomicon-quality continuation and fallback semantics; a defensible easy/test/hardening model; explicit Spellcraft escalation only for reusable composition; parent-child background-run isolation; the concrete subagent-strategy plus Whisper-page witness; accurate blocked and resumable behavior; browser-testable user control; and measurable route quality and overhead.
